author: Art
text:
So one needs to mark quite a few things on a chart. So I got this little tool (indicator developed) that helps me a lot every single day.

Functions:

Show spread:

On/Off Color Font

Extends rectangles:

Extends rectangles to current bar Option to choose how many bars rectangle is extended into the future Option to show rectangle edge prices Show text (it will always be located in the middle of screen/box no matter TF for convenience). Choose text color

Extends and straightens Trendlines:

Extends AND straightens trendlines within deviation to current bar Option to choose how many bars rectangle is extended into the future Exception color (exception color trendline will be straightened out but NOT extended) Deviation (difference in percentage between Start Price to End Price. If above deviation then indicator will not adjust the TL hence you can draw trendlines with the same tool)

Usually deviation 0.3 or 0.4 % solves the issue of using trendlines as horizontal lines and as casual trendlines as well. So one can mark important areas and see the origin easily and still use trendlines to mark other important stuff since we don't use trendlines per say in this nice community

What I do is create a template as you like, add indicator.. adjust all the settings. Then Save template as ¨Default¨ so next time you open any chart it has your layout + indicator set up and you can start doing your thing.

Short video on how it works and do not pay attention what was marked.

www.screencast.com/t/oDZEHOK9

If it helps you - use it, If it does not - delete it;-)

Cheers, Art

author: Art
text:
Have looked through my trading history since I joined RTM in around April 2015.

My trading has not changed probably even became worse. I pull off these grate trades and then multiple losses follow. I've worked markets but never worked on myself i.e. psychology. All my losses are nidicolous and not within my market understanding framework. I put trades that next day I'm ashamed off since they are so dumb.

The more time I spent looking at the screen - the worse it becomes. Best period were when I just joined RTM after 1 year break from trading, then after decent holiday or another period of time when I have not looked at charts.

I keep running in circles and that has to change.

I understand my losers and the reasons behind them. They are irrational trades that look very rational while in the moment of finding/trading them. Same mistakes happen again and again. Same mental patterns restrain me from being a successful trader.

I've worked my ass off to have the market understanding that I have. I pull off great trades hence it means I know how to do it. What I don't know how to and it boils down to CONSISTENCY. Consistency in trading, consistency in trading patterns.

It does piss me off since I've been doing it for maybe 6-7 years. I do my homework, I do review my trades, I use a LOT of time scrolling charts, preparing my charts for the next week etc etc.

To say the least IT HURTS LIKE HELL. I am my worst enemy. In the beginning I thought I will take a crack at the markets and see how it goes. No it seems I have no option but just to succeed.

I suppose it hurts so much because it is the same thing happening on every instrument, every timeframe every single day.

Just to summarise yesterday:

- Missed that AUDUSD opp... thought no biggy (but it did effect me in a very bad way later on) - AUDCHF long. Bad trade, traded long after there was a short signal. - Silver short. BE. Good management since price kept making HLs and did not manage to engulf key areas - AUDJPY Long. Jeez..... moronic trade idea. - CADJPY short. Winner. Very basic setup.

I need to simplify BIG TIME. Trade higher TFs. Avoid looking VLTF PA but instead trade the whole area.

I'm still reading through many great journals here and the best ones are so simple. I see the market same way until the moment I trade it.... then it gets messed up.

Anyway, done with this. Can't take this shit anymore. I have to become a consistent profitable trader.

author: ahdat
text: I feel ya buddy, your post is scarily similar to my story so far. Add to that I trade in PST (which is the absolute worse time zone to trade in) and most days I'm just trying to make a livable schedule and be awake enough to trade. Maybe we can trade notes on why we think we're lacking that consistency, I have a ton of thoughts. I think we KNOW what we need to do but we are lacking the DISCIPLINE to execute (including patience). I'm sure you can write a trading rulebook that will be profitable, but will have a hard time executing it with some level of consistency. We fall back to old habits when we are not balanced (and especially when we are stressed, whether from trading or some other area of our life). I think the key to all this is being able to override those bad habits (which is probably why I always hear If saying people that have never traded before have an easier time with RTM). Of course, this is difficult, but absolutely doable! Analogous to consistent exercise or eating a healthy diet. Even to breaking moderate addiction, like internet or gaming addiction. There are some great books out there about habit that really resonated to me in the context of trading. I'm going to try to slow down on my trading, stick with just a few pairs on M30+ time frames, and get back on forex tester instead of being glued to the M1 charts. I also notice i trade better after a break, which makes me think we struggle when we're too focused on trading and neglect the other areas of our lives. Need to find that balance. We're close man, I know we'll make it.

author: micka1
text:
In other words, once you're confronted to a live chart, you don't stick to your gameplan? is that it? Just a psychological issue? (is that what you meant by your "own worst enemy")...?

I'm more of a lurker, but i find your message kinda depressing...You sound kinda discouraged, tired of it all... If it's a technical issue....Then there's not much i can add here... But if your real problem is "psychological"... The only three things that have worked for me are:

1 - PATIENCE. (Never be afraid to miss trading opportunities. Always wait for the best possible entries, stick to the gameplan.)

2 - SELF CONTROL. (If you trade without any stress, you're more likely to respect the above...) And the only way is to diminish your lot size if you have to. And avoid revenge trades....If you don't do that, you'll start seeing set-ups everywhere...and you'll enter a vicious circle... I've noticed that many traders accumulate too many trades in a month.... Personally speaking, i used to have an average of 30 to 50 trades per month... Now only 15 to 10... (But they're bigger winners, so they compensate a lot).

3 - PRACTICE. Not just by reviewing the current market, but by also accelerating your pratice/progress curve with forextester for example...

Anyway, back to lurking...:)

text:
Hi Micka1,

I am very glad that you did not continue lurking after you saw my post. Your post made me think and that is already great.

I'll take it piece by piece so it is easier to address it.

n other words, once you're confronted to a live chart, you don't stick to your gameplan? is that it? Just a psychological issue? (is that what you meant by your "own worst enemy")...?

Exactly. Don't stick to my gameplan. When you say ¨only a psychological issue¨ I have a good laugh. It looks like a mountain and I can't see the peak yet.

Another matter, that is very closely related to this is me getting sucked into charts when I don't have trading opportunities around. I might start with smth like fresh supply on Daily and plan for short on H1 or H4( setup yet developing)... Then, all of a sudden, I wake up when I'm already long on M5 or M1 against that huge supply above. I'll adress it a bit later again.

1 -PATIENCE. (Never be afraid to miss trading opportunities. Always wait for the best possible entries, stick to the gameplan.)

I would like to say I am not afraid to miss trading opportunities but deep down that is fear #1 that I need to fix. I suppose I get desperate for not trading... that comes for upraising.. ¨work more - you'll have more¨.

2 - SELF CONTROL. (If you trade without any stress, you're more likely to respect the above...) And the only way is to diminish your lot size if you have to. And avoid revenge trades....If you don't do that, you'll start seeing set-ups everywhere...and you'll enter a vicious circle... I've noticed that many traders accumulate too many trades in a month.... Personally speaking, i used to have an average of 30 to 50 trades per month... Now only 15 to 10... (But they're bigger winners, so they compensate a lot).

Well looking at my history I do the same with higher lot size or smaller lot size. I don't think it is % loss in the account for actual losing process that gets me into the vicious circle you mentioned where I see setups everywhere.

Everyone says commit and change. I say the same in other matters. I have been saying to trade less to myself for quite some time now... few years actually. So.. HOW did change it mentally from 30-50 trades down to 10-15?

3 - PRACTICE. Not just by reviewing the current market, but by also accelerating your pratice/progress curve with forextester for example...

I have success with Forextester it changes with real markets. But I suppose these confidence/patience swings are becoming less and the only thing to do is to continue focusing on it. So these patience sings become so small that they disappear.

micka1, don't lurk. Participate. Your input helps.

author: Art
text:
Have started reading again Trading in the Zone by Douglas. Good stuff there. Did not connect with it when I read first time Ifew years back. I hope to brainwash myself here all possible ways.

Found a gold nugget in there. It went in the lines ¨If you have fear when you trade.. your brain is in flight or flight mode. In trading that means you do what is on your deepest levels... in my case ¨place a trade¨, other people might stall all the time or risk way too much etc¨. So brain excludes all the market info and chooses the facts that support the instinct ¨Trade It¨in my case. These are like very very dark sunglasses with a tiny hole in it them.. almost impossible to see through.

So reading and watching all kinds of videos lately on psychology found one trader discussing the personality type. He basically says there is a scale from scalper to position trader with day trader and swing trader in between those. In the beginning, we are better at one extreme or the other. He suggests to look not at trading but at other areas of life on decision making. Do you make decisions quick? can shift mental gears in seconds? then probably you fit in really well in scalping and day trading.

Another extreme is taking decisions slowly... When I thought about, it takes time for me to take a decision since I like to consider all options, outcomes and be ready. So by nature larger timeframes fit me better. Looking back at muy trading history all my good trades where on higher TFs.

He mentioned as well goal should be to become well rounded trader in all aspects. But one has to become really good at something before taking another step.

Ok. So figured this out.

Next. Pitfall lies in when I analyze higher TFs and a

a) I can't find setups for the near future so I go into lower timeframes.. and mess up usually. b) I need to define some zones on lower levels... after going a few timeframes down and marking what needs to marked... I get ¨stuck¨ there and start trading not just LTF but VLTF.

So all of a sudden I went from Unconscious Unconsciousness wen to Conscious Unconsciousness. Baby steps I suppose. Now when I feel bad I manage, in most cases, I cancel all trades and not look at charts for 2 days.

If anyone is reading here, I hope you are not bored to death with 1 man's psychological issues here. But it has to be addressed in this journey.

author: gizzo
text:
Art my friend, Its times like this that separate the losers from the winners.... When you fall, get up and go again. NEVER EVER give up! Then you will succeed, I can promise that. Imagaine the emotions you will have when you are standing at that mountain looking down on the looong path you have walked to reach for the top.

I have some small things that could help you

1. Use HTF, only use LTF for finetuning. 2. Only use Pending orders. Takes some emotions off. 3. Hide your moneybar in metatrader. less emotions...

4. DONT TRY TO HIT THAT HOMERUN. You are here to make money consistently. not to brag about crazy trades. Better to take profit earlier. 5. Look for areas where you can find footprints of IT:s trying to trick the market. Like QM-levels. 6. Take less trades and only the ones that you can explain for yourself why you will take it. 7. ALWAYS use SL. ALWAYS!

author: micka1
text:
@Art...

I went from 50 to 10/15 trades (sometimes 20 trades per month, it depends..) Just by being very (extremely) picky with my trades. So i end up avoiding many "potential" trades. (in other words, trades that look good but not picture perfect). And like i also said, "patience" is key. And when i say patience, i mean not touching a trade even if it goes against you after being in profit. Not reducing the lot size. (no partial closing, no trailing stops).

Personally speaking i rarely use any targets. (take profits). I sometimes manually move my stop loss, but only if the market sturcture allows it and if price is already distant from my entry. My trades usually last several hours, sometimes days...

Stylistically, i don't have a lot of new things to bring to this forum (but it's always interesting to see how others view the market). I don't trade that much differently than most of you guys. I use a lot of confluences for my trades (even though i could trade them fully "naked" on the chart). I use channels, Pivot points, SD, wait for traps. And occasionally use fibs.Most importantly, i only enter a position if the entry is ridiculously obvious. (That's another way to avoid over-trading).

So patience and discipline are very important. There should be no difference between forextester & a live chart. If you're still struggling on a live chart, (and again, if it's mostly a psychological problem), then change your bad habits. Do a checklist. We often lie to ourselves. People have a hard time admitting it, but it's part of human nature.

I don't know how to help you, i can only talk about my personal experience. What helped me (with my discipline, patience, sticking to my goals, having the mental strength)...Was not trading but losing weight and getting in shape. Losing my belly fat was a real nightmare

....But i was determined to do it.

Americans, Europeans etc.. Spend billions a year on weight-loss programs. Why? Because 90% of people don't have the discipline or patience to stick to their goals/gameplans. They always end up lying to themselves. You'll see the same problem with trading....Trading is just a different facet of the same thing...Smokers have the same problem..Alcoholics, drug addicts etc....All have a hard time with their bad habits. Once you've fixed this mental problem, then your live trades will mirror your demo/forextester results. The bad news..... It can take weeks, months, years...Before it happens.

PS: and yes, i have six pack abs now. lol
